summary: Bridget Allchin was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Cape Town. She founded the European Association of South Asian Archaeology and Art in 1970 and held a post at Wolfson College.
Brigitte Marschall studied at the University of Vienna from circa 1977 to 1982. She later served there as Professorin around 2003 and taught Mungunchimeg Batmunkh.

Bronislaw Malinowski studied at Jagiellonian University, Leipzig University, and under Charles Gabriel Seligman at LSE. He held positions at LSE (circa 1913–1938), Cornell (circa 1933), and Yale (circa 1939–1942), and taught Edmund Leach.

Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied at the universities of Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland. She held posts at the University of Auckland (~2009–2012), Marquette University (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014).

Brook Ziporyn works in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Chicago and under Donald J. Munro at the University of Michigan, later holding posts at Northwestern, Chicago, and the National University of Singapore.
Brooke Schedneck works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.

Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. His teachers included Edward H. Schafer, Michael Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, Akira Fujieda, and Noritoshi Aramaki.

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Sakya College in 1978 and earned his PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman, also studying under Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Lincoln is a religious studies, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian scholar. He studied at Haverford College and under Mircea Eliade at the University of Chicago, later holding posts at Minnesota (~1976–1993) and Chicago (~1993–2017).

Bruce Matthews works in religious studies and Buddhist studies, completing graduate studies at McMaster University (~1970–1974). He was a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Ceylon (~1971–1973) and served as Professor at Acadia University (~1976–2006).

Bruce McCoy Owens is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 1988) and has served as associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).
Bruno Dagens was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Colette Caillat. He served as a professor at KU Leuven from circa 1977 to 1986.
Bruno Galasek works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied under Franz Kielhorn (~1884–1886). He served as Professor Ordinarius at the University of Breslau (~1900–1921) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1921–1934).
Bruno Lindner was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Rudolf von Roth from circa 1876 to 1878 and held an academic post at Leipzig University from circa 1879 to 1923.

Bryan D. Lowe works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Otani University and under advisors including Jacqueline I. Stone and Martin Collcutt, and held a post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).

Bryan J. Cuevas works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Emory and the University of Virginia, held a postdoctoral fellowship at Princeton, and became John F. Priest Professor of Religion at Florida State University.
Bryce Ryan was a scholar who held posts at the University of Ceylon and Cornell University. During his career, he taught Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah.

Bulcsu Siklós is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles R. Bawden, and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996).
Bunkyo Aoki was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a disciple under Kozui Otani from circa 1908 to 1914 and held a post at the University of Tokyo from circa 1942 to 1946.
